translation_en: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir (Ibn Hazim) narrated to us: Ghaylan ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Qays ibn Riyah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: Whoever abandons obedience and separates from the community, then dies, dies a death of the pre-Islamic era. Whoever fights under a blind banner, becoming angry for tribal partisanship, calling to it, or supporting it, and is killed, his death is a death of the pre-Islamic era. Whoever rises against my community, striking its righteous and wicked alike, showing no restraint toward its believers and not honoring the covenant of anyone bound by a covenant, is not of me, and I am not of him.

Ubaydullah ibn Umar al-Qawariri narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Ziyad ibn Riyah al-Qaysi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said something like Jarir's hadith. He said: 'showing no restraint toward its believers.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Ziyad ibn Riyah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever abandons obedience and separates from the community, then dies, dies a death of the pre-Islamic era. Whoever is killed under a blind banner, out of anger for tribal partisanship and fighting for it, is not of my community. Whoever from my community rises against my community, striking its righteous and wicked alike, showing no restraint toward its believers and not honoring the covenant of anyone bound by its covenant, is not of me.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, with this chain. Ibn al-Muthanna did not mention the Prophet in the hadith, while Ibn Bashshar said in his version: The Messenger of Allah said something like their hadith.

Hasan ibn al-Rabi narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Jad (Abu Uthman), from Abu Raja, from Ibn Abbas, who related that the Messenger of Allah said: Whoever sees something he dislikes from his leader, let him be patient. Whoever separates from the community by even a handspan and dies in that state dies a death of the pre-Islamic era.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: al-Jad narrated to us: Abu Raja al-Utaridi narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Whoever dislikes something about his leader, let him be patient with him. No one separates from authority by even a handspan and dies in that state except that he dies a death of the pre-Islamic era.

Huraym ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us: al-Mutamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrate from Abu Mujliz, from Jundub ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever is killed beneath a blind banner, calling to tribal partisanship or supporting it, dies a death of the pre-Islamic era.

Ubaydullah ibn Muadh al-Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Asim (Ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd) narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Muhammad, from Nafi, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar came to Abdullah ibn Muti when the events at al-Harrah took place during the time of Yazid ibn Muawiyah. Ibn Muti said: Put a cushion down for Abu Abd al-Rahman. Ibn Umar said: I did not come to sit. I came to tell you a hadith I heard the Messenger of Allah say. I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Whoever removes a hand from obedience will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection with no argument in his favor. Whoever dies without a pledge of allegiance upon his neck dies a death of the pre-Islamic era.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Jafar, from Bukayr ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashajj, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, that he came to Ibn Muti. He mentioned a report like it from the Prophet.

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jablah narrated to us: Bishr ibn Umar narrated to us. Both said: Hisham ibn Sad narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, with the meaning of Nafi's hadith from Ibn Umar.

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me. Ibn Nafi said: Gundar narrated to us; Ibn Bashshar said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, who said: I heard Arfajah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: There will be disturbances and events. Whoever seeks to divide the affair of this community while it is united, strike him with the sword, whoever he may be.

Ahmad ibn Khirash narrated to us: Habban narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us. [Another chain:] al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated to me: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Shayban. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Musab ibn al-Miqdam al-Khathami narrated to us: Israil narrated to us. [Another chain:] Hajjaj narrated to me: Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Abdullah ibn al-Mukhtar and a man whose name he mentioned narrated to us. All report it from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, from Arfajah, from the Prophet, with a similar report; in all of their narrations it says: 'Kill him.'

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me: Yunus ibn Abi Yafur narrated to us, from his father, from Arfajah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Whoever comes to you while your affair is united under one man, seeking to split your unity or divide your community, kill him.

Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wasiti narrated to me: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadr, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: When allegiance has been given to two caliphs, kill the latter of them.

Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdi narrated to us: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Dabbah ibn Mihsan, from Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah said: There will be leaders; you will recognize some of what they do and disapprove of some. Whoever recognizes the right is free of blame, and whoever disapproves is safe. But whoever is pleased and follows them... They said: Should we not fight them? He said: No, so long as they pray.

Abu Ghassan al-Mismai and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, both from Muadh; the wording is Abu Ghassan's. Muadh (Ibn Hisham al-Dastawai) narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Dabbah ibn Mihsan al-Anazi, from Umm Salamah, the Prophet's wife, from the Prophet, who said: Leaders will be appointed over you. You will recognize some of what they do and disapprove of some. Whoever detests it is free of blame, and whoever disapproves is safe; but whoever is pleased and follows them... They said: Messenger of Allah, should we not fight them? He said: No, so long as they pray. That is, whoever detests it in his heart and disapproves of it in his heart.

Abu al-Rabi al-Ataki narrated to me: Hammad (Ibn Zayd) narrated to us: al-Mualla ibn Ziyad and Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Dabbah ibn Mihsan, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said something similar, except that he said: Whoever disapproves is free of blame, and whoever detests it is safe.

Hasan ibn al-Rabi al-Bajali narrated this to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, from Dabbah ibn Mihsan, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said a similar report, but he did not mention: 'But whoever is pleased and follows them.'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us: al-Awzai narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Ruzaq ibn Hayyan, from Muslim ibn Qarazah, from Awf ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: The best of your leaders are those whom you love and who love you, and for whom you pray and who pray for you. The worst of your leaders are those whom you hate and who hate you, and whom you curse and who curse you. It was asked: Messenger of Allah, should we not oppose them with the sword? He said: No, so long as they establish the prayer among you. When you see something from your rulers that you dislike, dislike their deed, but do not withdraw your hand from obedience.

Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us: al-Walid (Ibn Muslim) narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us: A freedman of Banu Fazara—Ruzaq ibn Hayyan—informed me that he heard Muslim ibn Qarazah, cousin of Awf ibn Malik al-Ashjai, say: I heard Awf ibn Malik al-Ashjai say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: The best of your leaders are those whom you love and who love you, and for whom you pray and who pray for you. The worst of your leaders are those whom you hate and who hate you, and whom you curse and who curse you. We said: Messenger of Allah, should we oppose them then? He said: No, so long as they establish the prayer among you—no, so long as they establish the prayer among you. Whoever has a governor over him and sees him doing something disobedient to Allah, let him dislike the disobedience he commits, but let him not withdraw his hand from obedience. Ibn Jabir said: When Ruzaq narrated this to me, I asked him: I adjure you by Allah, Abu al-Miqdam, did Muslim ibn Qarazah tell you this, saying that he heard Awf say that he heard the Messenger of Allah? He knelt on his knees, faced the qiblah, and said: Yes, by Allah, the One besides whom there is no god! I heard it from Muslim ibn Qarazah, who said he heard Awf ibn Malik say that he heard the Messenger of Allah.

Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Ibn Jabir narrated to us with this chain, and he said that Ruzaq was a freedman of Banu Fazara. Muslim said: Muawiyah ibn Salih also reported it from Rabiah ibn Yazid, from Muslim ibn Qarazah, from Awf ibn Malik, from the Prophet, with a similar report.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Layth ibn Sad narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we numbered one thousand four hundred. We pledged allegiance to him while Umar held his hand beneath the tree, which was a samurah tree. He said: We pledged that we would not flee. We did not pledge allegiance to die.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: We did not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah to die; we pledged allegiance to him not to flee.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir being asked how many they were on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: We were fourteen hundred. We pledged allegiance to him while Umar held his hand beneath the tree, which was a samurah tree. We all pledged except Judd ibn Qays al-Ansari's grandfather, who hid beneath the belly of his camel.

Ibrahim ibn Dinar narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-Awar, the freedman of Sulayman ibn Mijlid, narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir being asked whether the Prophet took a pledge at Dhu al-Hulayfah. He said: No. He prayed there, but he took a pledge beneath a tree only at the tree of al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Prophet supplicated at the well of al-Hudaybiyyah.

Said ibn Amr al-Ashathi, Suwayd ibn Said, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ahmad ibn Abdah narrated to us; the wording is Said's. Said and Ishaq said: Sufyan informed us; the other two said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we numbered one thousand four hundred. The Prophet said to us: You are the best people on earth today. Jabir said: If I could see, I would show you the place of the tree.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, who said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about the people of the tree. He said: If we had been one hundred thousand, that would have been enough for us. We were one thousand five hundred.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr said: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us. [Another chain:] Rifaa ibn al-Haytham narrated to us: Khalid (al-Tahhan) narrated to us. Both said: Husayn narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, from Jabir, who said: If we had been one hundred thousand, that would have been enough for us. We were one thousand five hundred.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ishaq said: He informed us; Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, who said: Salim ibn Abi al-Jad narrated to me: I asked Jabir how many you were that day. He said: One thousand four hundred.

Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Amr (Ibn Murrah), who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa narrated to me: The people of the tree were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam constituted one-eighth of the Emigrants.
